description:
There's a Moon Spraying Its Ocean Into Space

Saturn's moon Enceladus hides a salty ocean under its ice and blasts it into space through giant geysers. Cassini flew right through them and found the ingredients for life.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

Images: NASA, ESA, ESO and Wikimedia Commons (free licenses, credited in the video file's notes)
Narration: AI voice

#enceladus #saturn #space #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: There's a moon out there spraying its own ocean into space.
It's called Enceladus, a tiny white moon of Saturn, only about five hundred kilometers wide.
segments.headline: Saturn's tiny moon

segments.text: Under its icy shell is a hidden ocean of salty water.
segments.headline: An ocean under the ice

segments.text: And at its south pole, cracks in the ice blast that water out as giant geysers.
segments.headline: Geysers into space

segments.text: So NASA did something wild. The Cassini spacecraft flew straight through the spray, and tasted it.
segments.headline: Cassini tasted it

segments.text: It found salt, organic molecules, and in 2023, phosphorus. Ingredients life on Earth needs.
Nobody has found life there. But it's one of the best places in the solar system to look.
segments.headline: Is something living there?

segments.text: Next stop: The Oort Cloud. Should we send a mission to look for life there? Yes or no in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
